requirement:
HC represents a GitHub issue by a stable owner, repository, and issue-number
identity. Reading the node supplies the issue's title, opening post, and
open/closed status as one snapshot. HC computes its fingerprint and formatted
text from that supplied snapshot through `Domain`.

For illustration:

```rust,ignore
struct GithubIssueContents {
    title: String,
    opening_post: String,
    status: IssueStatus,
}

enum IssueStatus {
    Open,
    Closed,
}
```
rationale:
The subject's obligations are: (1) a GitHub issue node has a stable owner/repo/issue-number identity; (2) reading the node supplies title, opening post and open/closed status as one snapshot; (3) the fingerprint and formatted text come from that supplied snapshot through `Domain`. The `.inputs`, `.open` and `.cache` refinements and `.related` carry their own tests and need none here.

The reviewed test is `src/sdk/issues.rs#mod[tests]/fn[tracked_issue_status_and_fingerprints_follow_refreshed_redacted_snapshots]`. It covers the obligations as follows.

- **Identity:** it interns `HabeasNode::GithubIssue(ISSUE)` and asserts `node_path` is `["github", ISSUE]`. Identity is the owner/repo#number string, and the test shows it as a stable path. Re-interning the same string is cache behaviour that the text does not single out.
- **One snapshot:** it parses the supplied text, which is the issue name, a newline and a JSON snapshot. It asserts the `title`, `status` ("open") and `opening_post` fields. The post is the redacted text, which the `.inputs` refinement covers. `github.count()==1` after verify and `node_content` shows a single fetch served the whole snapshot.
- **Fingerprint:** it asserts the verification dependency is `Dependency::Node(issue, supplied.fingerprint())`. It then changes title, body and state one at a time, and after each expiry asserts `check_inputs` turns false (with the field name as the message). So the fingerprint depends on each snapshot component, including open/closed status.
- **Formatted text:** it asserts `supplied.format()` omits the token. After each refresh it asserts the formatted text contains the new title, post and `closed` value, and it asserts the verified output matches the open/closed state.

I found no requirement-violating behaviour that these assertions would accept.
